title: Terraform module: HSM-backed secrets orchestrator (Vault & Secrets Manager bridge)
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) customers require a Terraform-level, production-safe module to provision and manage secrets backed by HSM/KMS and reliably sync or bridge those secrets into either cloud Secrets Manager (for local platform components) or HashiCorp Vault (for customer-managed secret stores). Current ad-hoc setups create drift, unclear rotation procedures, and fragile IAM/grant logic.

Goal: Deliver a reusable Terraform module that: (1) provisions KMS keys or HSM-backed key resources, (2) manages secret objects and rotation hooks, (3) creates least-privilege roles/policies for runtime services, and (4) optionally bridges secrets between Vault and Secrets Manager with safe migration and health-checks. The module must be idempotent, support in-place upgrades, and provide health-check outputs for our deployment automation and alerting.
acceptance_criteria:
- Module publishes inputs/outputs documented in README and example usage for AWS (KMS + CloudHSM) and HashiCorp Vault; provider-agnostic hooks documented.
- Supports two modes: (A) platform-managed secrets (Secrets Manager) with HSM/KMS CMKs and (B) customer-managed Vault path provisioning with wrapped keys.
- Rotation implemented as a Terraform-driven state + safe handoff (rotate-key -> re-encrypt -> update secret consumers) with no downtime for consumers in Canary test.
- All created IAM roles/policies use least privilege and are testable via unit/integration Terraform tests.
- Health-check output includes key status, last-rotation timestamp, last-sync timestamp, and an explicit lint status for IAM grants.
- Security review completed and automated acceptance tests passing in our CI (unit + acceptance).
technical_notes:
Design decisions and details:
- Module split into three submodules: key_provisioning, secret_store_bridge, and health_checks. This keeps AWS-specific code isolated from Vault glue.
- Key provisioning: support aws_kms_key (with key_spec compatible with HSM backing when running in Dedicated/on-prem CloudHSM), and an extensible provider hook for external HSM (PKCS#11) via a 'key_provider' interface variable.
- Secret store modes: 'secrets_manager', 'vault', 'bridge'. 'bridge' creates a pull-sync Lambda (or container task) that can be deployed as part of Private stack to mirror secrets from Vault to Secrets Manager or vice versa depending on signing/trust model.
- Rotation: Terraform cannot do live re-encrypt; we implement a two-phase pattern: create a new key, add grants to consumers, run a re-encrypt job (ad-hoc CI job or reconcile container), then revoke old key. Module exposes outputs to trigger orchestration.
- IAM: create fine-grained service principals and use condition keys (aws:SourceIp, aws:VpcEndpoint) where applicable. Provide optional overrides for existing roles.
- Health checks: Terraform outputs a JSON blob (string) with key and sync metadata; an external monitor (console agent) will hit the module output endpoint in deploy pipeline and convert to metrics.
- Backwards compatibility: accept legacy naming patterns via input mapping; keep state migration notes in README.
- Upgrade strategy: maintain lifecycle rules in resources to avoid accidental recreation; use 'create_before_destroy' where needed for key rotation flows.
migration_plan:
1) Inventory current secrets and keys (existing Terraform state + runtime secrets). 2) Run module in 'dry-run' mode to validate IAM and naming collisions. 3) For each secret: create new HSM-backed key (without deleting old), provision temporary grants, run re-encrypt job to copy secret ciphertext under new key, update consumers to reference new secret ARN/path, revoke old grants, then remove old key after a retention window. 4) For Vault -> Secrets Manager bridge: enable bridge in staging, run sync with verification checksums, and incrementally enable consumers. 5) Rollout via canary in a single VPC then escalate to full fleet.

Notes: Provide rollback by preserving old key and maintaining dual-read mode in consumers for 48h before key retirement.
test_plan:
- Unit: Terratest + kitchen-terraform mocks for IAM policy linting and resource graph verification.
- Integration: spin up ephemeral AWS account with CloudHSM (or simulated HSM using KMS multi-region keys) and run full lifecycle: create key, provision secret, rotate, bridge to Vault, and assert that consumers can still decrypt.
- CI: acceptance job that runs against a staging Private cluster; health-check output must be printed and parsed.
- Failure scenarios: simulate grant misconfiguration, network partition to Vault, and rotation step failure. Module must leave system in a recoverable state and surface actionable error messages.
- Metrics: collect time-to-sync, number-of-retries, and rotation-duration for each test run.
